newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison CEO says no regrets over strategy.
newsitem.headline: Morrison CEO says no regrets over strategy.

text.p: Gordon Stollery, chairman and chief executive of takeover target Morrison Petroleums Ltd, said on Thursday he had no regrets over business strategies that ultimately placed Morrison in play.

In an media briefing, a small army of Morrison executives, financial advisers and lawyers outlined how the company pursued long-term gas exploration and development prospects in northern and southern Alberta while working to reduce debt levels with asset sales.
"That was what I believed was in the longer best interest of the company," Stollery said.
"I don't think you can run a company just to try and avoid takeover bids."

He said Morrison's stock price had yet to reflect potential new production and had suffered following drilling difficulties at the much-watched Racehorse Creek well in the Alberta foothills before Canadian 88 Energy Corp launched its C$652 million hostile bid earlier this month.
Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash, to a maximum of C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.

Company officials on Thursday described landholdings and drilling plans in the gas-rich areas of Northern Alberta, where Morrison has 541,000 net acres and will soon operate five gas plants, and southwestern Alberta, where it controls 153,000 acres with a geological potential of up to 1.5 trillion cubic feet of gas.

The southwestern area, known for potential large reserves and deep, complex and expensive drilling, is seen as the key prize in Canadian 88's advance. Morrison's board has urged shareholders to reject the bid saying that it fails to recognize the company's production and reserve potential.

Stollery also took aim at Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval for not providing both companies' shareholders with fresh information regarding its own financial and operating standing, which he said was necessary for the share-swap portion of the offer.

Of particular importance, he said, was more detailed data on Canadian 88's Waterton foothills gas discovery, reported on Thursday as having production potential of 10 million cubic feet per day from one geological zone and 18-22 MMCFD from another.

"If our shareholders are even remotely considering taking their shares in exchange, they would need to know the financial results for (Canadian) 88 for the last year, the engineering results and have a straight answer on their well in Waterton," he said, adding that he knew of no investors tendering to the bid.
"I think our shareholders are entitled to appropriate information on the currency of exchange in this transaction -- that is one of our major concerns."
Stollery said there was "a reasonable chance" of Morrison surviving as an independent firm with a restructuring, but said it was too early to predict the outcome of the battle.
He also repeated that interest in the firm from potential white knights remained strong and "several" visits had been made to the company's confidential data room.
What he did rule out, however, was Morrison launching a reverse takeover for Canadian 88.
Canadian 88, for its next salvo in the takeover battle, has invited reporters for its own briefing on Friday.
